lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Late. The fire escape, two mugs, the city humming below.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: You came home quiet again. Third time this week.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They don't rush to fill the silence. You respect that in a person.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: You count sirens, you know. In your sleep. Under your breath.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Somebody should keep track of you for a change.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The city hums. They set their mug down, careful, deliberate.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: The job takes pieces of you some nights. Where do they go?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Nobody's ever asked it like that.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You talk until the streetlights buzz off. Voices you couldn't save. Ones you did.

lines.speaker: partner
lines.text: Thank you for trusting me with them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They hold your coffee so your hands are free to shake. It helps.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It's the truest thing you've said all week. You both know it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The city hums. Nobody moves for a long time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: 'Fine.' The word every operator knows means the opposite.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: They let it go, this time. The space between you keeps its exact width.
